questions.q: What determines whether a Payment Process Request generates a printed check or an electronic file?
options: The supplier chooses at the time of payment
The format configured on the Payment Process Profile used for that run
The invoice's matching type
A random selection by the system
questions.explain: The PPP is set up in advance to point at a specific output format, whether a check layout or a given electronic file format.

questions.q: Which electronic file format is commonly used for US domestic ACH transfers?
options: BAI2
NACHA
SWIFT MT103
questions.explain: NACHA is the standard format for US domestic ACH payment files.

questions.q: Where is ISO 20022 most commonly used?
options: As an international standard, especially common for SEPA transfers in Europe
Only for check printing
Only for payroll in the United States
Exclusively for bank statement reconciliation
questions.explain: ISO 20022 is a widely adopted international payment file standard, prominent in European SEPA transfers.

questions.q: What is a positive pay file used for?
options: Converting electronic payments into paper checks
Listing issued checks so the bank can verify a presented check matches before honoring it
Calculating withholding tax on a payment
Reconciling the general ledger to the subledger
questions.explain: Positive pay is a fraud-prevention file sent to the bank listing every check issued, compared against checks presented for payment.

questions.q: Why doesn't positive pay apply to electronic payments like EFT or wire?
options: Electronic payments are always more expensive to process
Electronic payments cannot be verified by banks at all
Positive pay is only available outside the United States
Electronic payments don't carry the same forgery/alteration risk that paper checks do
questions.explain: Positive pay exists specifically to catch forged or altered paper checks, a risk that doesn't apply the same way to electronic transfers.
